target: Give ctxToImp a computable definition so the four context-based Decidable instances for the propositional sequent calculi stop being noncomputable
summary: Four-phase sequential plan implementing Route 3 (Quotient.recOnSubsingleton) from the verified-prototype research report. Phase 1 edits LJ/Decidability.lean: adds the named public helper ljListDerivableDecidable, rewrites instDecidableLJDerivable's body to eliminate from the Multiset quotient underlying Gamma.val into the Subsingleton Decidable, drops noncomputable from both LJ instances, and corrects five docstring sites that misattribute the cause to Finset.toList. Phase 2 does the structurally identical LK edit, minus the letI universe bridge (instDecidableTautologyTableau is not universe-pinned). Phase 3 creates CslibTests/ContextDecidability.lean with #guard_msgs in #eval assertions covering the task's target case ({p, p->q} |- q) plus negative cases and the LJ/LK excluded-middle contrast, and registers it alphabetically in the CslibTests.lean barrel. Phase 4 re-baselines the axiom-census exact-set ratchet (expected diff: exactly one added line for the LJ helper; the LK helper must NOT appear) and runs the full six-step CSLib CI order. The plan explicitly does NOT attempt the task title's literal ask: a computable ctxToImp at its current type is mathematically impossible, so ctxToImp and the four Finset-level deduction defs stay noncomputable with corrected docstrings stating the reason is inherent rather than incidental. Verification tiers: interface for phases 1-3 (each builds its changed module plus its enumerated direct dependent), full for phase 4. Every phase carries a Scope Hypothesis with a mechanical confirmation command.

artifacts.summary: Four-phase sequential implementation plan: LJ instances, LK instances, executable #eval conformance tests, axiom-census re-baseline plus full CI sweep

decisions_made: ADOPTED Route 3 verbatim from the research report rather than re-deriving it: the report is a verified prototype (compiled with lake env lean against the live tree, evaluated correctly on 11 expressions), so the phases transcribe known-good code instead of exploring.

SPLIT the work by file (LJ, then LK) rather than by concern (all code, then all docstrings). Each Decidability file is one agent run, and docstring corrections in a file ride along with that file's code edit so a single module build covers both.

MADE Phase 2 depend on Phase 1 even though the two files are edited independently: LK/Decidability.lean imports LJ/Decidability.lean, so Phase 1's interface-tier verification already builds LK, and running them in parallel would create a territory conflict for no gain.

ASSIGNED interface tier (not local) to Phases 1-3: each changes a module with at least one enumerated direct dependent (LJ -> LK; the test module -> the CslibTests barrel), and the tie-break rule says take the stricter tier when uncertain. Phase 4 is full.

GAVE every phase a Scope Hypothesis with a mechanical confirmation command, because every phase asserts a count: 3 retained noncomputable markers in LJ, 2 in LK, exactly 2 files touched in Phase 3, and exactly 1 added baseline line in Phase 4.

PROMOTED the axiom-census re-baseline to its own phase rather than a task inside the CI sweep. It is the plan's highest-value scope hypothesis: an unexpectedly large diff is the primary signal that the change perturbed something beyond its verified-nil blast radius, and it needs an explicit inspect-before-commit gate.

CARRIED the three recorded implementation traps into phase task text as MUST NOTs rather than leaving them in the report: the named helper (the inlined variant provably does not elaborate), the List.toFinset_eq orientation (the .symm form fails with a type mismatch), and the LJ-only letI universe bridge (must not be added to LK by analogy).

MANDATED #guard_msgs in #eval and forbade decide in Phase 3, with the reason recorded inline so an implementer hitting the decide failure does not conclude the construction is broken -- the kernel error shows it unfolds through the new instance and helper and stalls only at the pre-existing WellFounded.fix.
STATED as an explicit Non-Goal that ctxToImp itself is not made computable, so the plan is not later read as having silently dropped the task title's literal ask.
notes: The plan passes scripts/validate-artifact.sh in --strict mode with 0 warnings. Blast radius is verified nil (zero references to the affected declarations outside the two Decidability files), so each phase is independently revertable to a green build. Two out-of-scope items are named explicitly so the implementer does not drift into them: the two FMP decidability defs (noncomputable via Fintype.ofInjective, an unrelated irreducible cause) and the two pre-existing unusedDecidableInType lint warnings in this subtree. The Route 3 shape is recorded as transferable to the LM/minimal-logic decidability follow-on, which should inherit the computable route rather than the Finset.toList taint.
